name: Clonidine

lead: Clonidine is a prescription alpha-2 agonist used for high blood pressure, and in extended-release form for ADHD in children and adolescents. On looksmax.org one thread reposts a suggestion to combine it with pregnenolone and cyproheptadine for stress, with the aim of calmer nights and a more rested look.

It activates alpha-2 receptors in the brainstem, lowering sympathetic nervous system output, heart rate and vascular resistance. No published study has tested that combination or clonidine for appearance.

paras: Medically it is taken on a prescribed schedule for blood pressure or ADHD. Forum users mention it within stress and sleep stacks alongside other compounds.
The label reports dry mouth, drowsiness, dizziness and constipation, and warns that abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound high blood pressure. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Forum posters include clonidine in stress stacks with pregnenolone and cyproheptadine, aiming for lower stress, calmer nights and a more rested look. It is a prescription blood-pressure and ADHD drug.

lead: Clonidine is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist. The US label for the tablets lists hypertension as the indication [1]. Extended-release forms are approved for ADHD in children and adolescents [2].

In looksmaxxing-adjacent forums it appears in discussions of stress, sleep and 'dopamine' protocols; one looksmax.org thread reposts a forum user's suggestion to combine pregnenolone, clonidine and cyproheptadine for stress and attention problems [3]. No published trial has tested such a combination or clonidine for appearance outcomes.
Common adverse effects on the label include dry mouth, drowsiness and dizziness, and the label warns against abrupt discontinuation because of rebound hypertension [1].

paras: The label lists treatment of hypertension, alone or with other antihypertensives [1]. Grokipedia reports that clonidine was developed as a nasal decongestant, then repurposed after its blood-pressure-lowering and sedating effects were seen in early human testing, and introduced for hypertension in 1974 [2]. It is also used as add-on in resistant hypertension, according to the same source [2]. A Veterans Affairs study compared six antihypertensive drugs including clonidine with placebo [4].

Extended-release clonidine is FDA-approved for ADHD in ages 6 to 17, alone or with stimulants [2]. A network meta-analysis of ADHD drugs includes clonidine among non-stimulant options [5]. A Cochrane network meta-analysis of smoking-cessation drugs also considered clonidine among other therapies [6].

Clonidine stimulates alpha-2 receptors in the brainstem, reducing sympathetic outflow, heart rate and peripheral resistance [2]. Early work reported inhibition of noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons in the brain [7].

The label reports dry mouth in about 40 of 100 patients, drowsiness in about 33, dizziness in about 16, and constipation and sedation in about 10 each [1]. Sudden cessation has resulted in nervousness, agitation, headache, tremor and a rapid rise in blood pressure [1]. Grokipedia notes hypotension, bradycardia and angioedema as more serious risks [2].

A looksmax.org thread reposts advice from a Ray Peat-influenced forum user suggesting pregnenolone, clonidine and cyproheptadine to lower stress and address attention problems [3]. This is anecdotal forum advice and not a studied regimen.

Trials of clonidine are summarized in meta-analyses for ADHD and smoking cessation and in the 1993 Veterans Affairs hypertension comparison [4][5][6]. No studies were found testing clonidine, alone or in the forum combination described above, for stress-related appearance outcomes.
